newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty firms vs basket on foreign speculation.
newsitem.headline: Zloty firms vs basket on foreign speculation.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed some half a percentage point against the basket of currencies in early trade on foreign speculative buying but dealers said its gains were capped by profit taking.
They said foreign players bought zlotys at around -2.0 percent from the parity rate pushing the Polish unit up, but then sold it at around -1.3 percent from parity.

"There is very little trade in T-bills or T-bonds. It is mainly speculation which is likely to keep the zloty framed between -1.0 and -2.0 percent from parity," said Wojciech Kowalczyk debt dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

At 0830 GMT the zloty was at -1.40/-1.56 percent from the trading band centre against -2.0/-2.20 at the opening. It was at 3.4450/00 against the dollar and 1.8840/75 against the mark against 3.4500/640 and 1.8950/90 at opening respectively.

Some dealers said the rise in Polish net currency reserves in June by $941 million to $22.65 billion announced on Tuesday as well as more information on the government's flood relief programme were positive singals for Poland.
They said other factors, such as the country's growing current account gap and a rise in inflation in June still kept foreign investors from returning in numbers.

On the money market one-day rates eased some 0.2 point to 23.25/23.45 percent for O/N and 23.36/23.93 percent for T/N since morning even though the National Bank of Poland offered to drain 400 million zlotys for six and 14 days and sell 700 million zlotys of its 91-day bills.

Dealers said the market would keenly watch the maximum reverse repo and the 91-day rates accepted by the central bank in view of the NBP's recent comments that it would raise rates to offset the monetary effect of its 2.5 billion zloty flood relief loan to the government.
